In another column of our paper will be found the advertisement of our friend, Mr. Wm. Still, who was formerly, we believe, the Secretary in the Anti-Slavery Office in this city. articles.headline: Obituary: Catherine A. Wiggins
articles.summary: Rev. Elisha Weaver--Dear Sir: It becomes our painful duty to record the death of our beloved sister, Catherine A. Wiggins, who died on Sunday evening, June 16th, 1861, in full hope of a blessed immortality. Sister Wiggins was a member of Bethel Church for twenty-three years... during her protracted illness of nearly six months of consumption of the lungs...
people: deceased, d. Sunday evening June 16, 1861, of consumption; member of Bethel Church 23 years

articles.headline: Inaugural and Prospectus
articles.summary: To the Readers of the Christian Recorder:--Dear Friends; Previous to the rise of the New England Annual Conference, sitting in Bethel Church, Meeting St., Providence, R. I., from Thursday, the 13th, to Thursday, the 20th of June, our Father and Bishop, the Rev. Willis Nazrey, appointed your unworthy servant to the pastoral charge of Little Wesley Station, City of Philadelphia, and as the chief editor of this, your much loved sheet... In company with my wife, I left Providence on Tuesday, the 2d of July...
people: new chief editor and pastor of Little Wesley Station (inferred author; the piece is unsigned, but the same page names him as chief editor and minister of Little Wesley)

articles.headline: News from the Churches (Trenton Circuit)
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: On Wednesday, June 12th, 1861, we arrived home in Trenton, the Capital city of the State of New Jersey, and the headquarters of Trenton Circuit, having attended two Annual Conferences, since May the 18th of this year. In looking back over the past history of our experience in the African Methodist Episcopal itinerant service, twenty-three years, we have arrived at the conclusion that we have not met with more agreeable sessions of the Philadelphia Conference for a dozen or score of years than the last...

articles.author: Elisha Weaver

articles.headline: Impostors
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: There are some scamps making a living under the garb of the Christian Recorder... Said Impostor has collected money from these white friends... In relation to agents, our ministers who are appointed in charge of circuits and stations, are agents in their fields of labour... All letters relating to the business of the Recorder, or Book Concern, should be directed to Rev. E. Weaver, Box [number not verified], Phila., Pa. articles.headline: Obituary: Sister Charlotte, of Bethel and Wesley churches
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: The following is an obituary on the life, character and death of Sister Charlotte (her surname is illegible in the heading; her husband's reads William Middleton), the daughter of William and Sarah P--- (surname faint), residing in Elkton, State of Delaware [sic, as printed], where Charlotte was born, in the eighth month, A. M. E. (Bethel) Church, in Sixth Street. After some time had elapsed she transferred her membership to Wesley Church, in Hurst Street, in which connexion she continued until her death a worthy member. Sister Charlotte was married to William Middleton [VERIFY] on the 21st of the 3d month, by the Rev. Walter Proctor...
people: former pastor, writer of the obituary (Rev.)

articles.headline: From Our General Book Steward
articles.author: E. Weaver
articles.summary: Dear Brother Standford:--I suppose you have been on the look-out for something from me. Well, I thought, before I left the "smoky city," I would give you and the readers of the Recorder a short account of the incidents connected with my journey. I left home on the 23d ultimo, at half-past 9 o'clock at night, and ... conveyed us to the depot, at the corner of Eleventh and Market Streets ... Having secured our tickets, Miss A. Hinton [VERIFY], accompanied by Mr. W. W. Whipper ... started a-head of me. Dated Pittsburgh, July 29th [VERIFY day], 1861. Describes Jim Crow car segregation on the Pennsylvania railroad out of Philadelphia, then visits to Lewistown, Huntingdon, Altoona, Pittsburgh and Allegheny (Rev. S. T. Jones, Allen Chapel, Rev. S. Watts of Wylie St. Church, Prof. Freeman of the Allegheny school; these western Pennsylvania names are text only).
people: Philadelphia friend who saw Miss H. to the cars and got her a berth in the sleeping car

articles.headline: A Sin That Needs Rebuke (letter on picnic excursions)
articles.author: D.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--If ever there was a sin that needed rebuke, it is the sin of needless extravagance and waste. In these days when the country is amidst the horrors of civil strife ... it is a sin that needs rebuke to see large parties of colored people spending hundreds of dollars in pic-nic excursions, when it is a pleasure--if pleasure it be--that white people, whose resources are greater than ours, are not able to enjoy.

articles.headline: Affliction (second sermon of the course, Little Wesley)
articles.summary: Second sermon of the course on affliction (continuation of the series begun at Little Wesley Chapel). Subject--A reason why we should bear our affliction with resignation; because we have a compassionate High Priest.

articles.headline: Editorial paragraphs (acting editor; Harvest Home at Trenton; acknowledgment)

Williams, and brother Winder, which should have been published last week; but their being received at a late period, and I being compelled to leave the city on Tuesday, the 30th ult., with a sick member of my family, prevented their publication. We were also informed of a grand Harvest Home to be held in Trenton, under the pastoral charge of Rev. J. P. Campbell, on Thursday, the 8th ult. [sic] ... The acting editor ("chief editor of the Christian Recorder for the time being") also endorses Campbell's rebuke of the corresponding editors.

articles.headline: News from the Churches. From our Corresponding Editor of Philadelphia District
articles.author: J. P. C.
articles.summary: The Quarterly Meeting of the Society at Louisville [VERIFY place] came off at that place on Sunday last. There was in attendance a large concourse of people, gathered together from the neighboring towns and villages, so that we could not accommodate them within doors, and had to address them without ... At [half-past 10 or 11?] o'clock, A.M., we had a very instructive discourse ... by that venerable and very useful old servant of God, Rev. articles.headline: Letter from Canada West
articles.author: Parker T. Smith
articles.summary: Dresden, C. W., August 2d, 1861. Rev. and Dear Sir:--From the interest manifested by me for the success of your paper, while in the city of Philadelphia, it would seem strange did I not communicate with you from the place which I have chosen as a home, beyond the limits of the United States ... When I commenced to write a series of ethnological articles for the Christian Recorder, some months ago, I had not the remotest idea of being here at this time ... We left Philadelphia on Friday afternoon at a quarter past 3 o'clock, 5th ult., and arrived in Chatham, C. W., on Sabbath morning. Describes politics, separate schools, and a flourishing Lodge of Odd Fellows (Prince Albert Lodge) at Dresden: 'members of the Order in Philadelphia will be pleased to know that they are progressing finely.'

articles.headline: Affliction, continued (fourth sermon of the course, Wesley Church, Hurst Street)
articles.summary: The 4th sermon of the course was delivered in Wesley church, Hurst street, on Sabbath evening, the 18th inst. The congregation was much larger than on any previous occasion ... The above discourse was succeeded by an appeal to sinners, plain and pointed in the way of an exhortation, by Rev. J. R. V. Morgan. After which a prayer was addressed to the throne of grace by Rev. H. Davis. The next sermon of the course will be delivered next Sabbath evening, at 8 o'clock. Subject: The Weaned Child.

articles.headline: A Few Words in Behalf of the Christian Recorder
articles.summary: Dear brethren, ministers, members and friends, of the A. M. E. connexion, permit me to ask an important question. The question is this: should this, our paper, The Christian Recorder, fail to exist one year, what would be the cause of such a failure? ... Predictions ... would loudly cry, "Stanford's and Weaver's paper has failed." ... The chief doers of Philadelphia District, I speak of ministers having circuits and stations out of the city, are J. P. Campbell, who sells twenty-five copies, weekly, R. Harney, T. Gould, and one or two others nearly the same number. Also criticizes money spent on camp meetings in the Philadelphia District.
people: minister, Philadelphia District; sells 25 copies weekly (Rev.)
minister with circuit out of the city, Philadelphia District

articles.headline: News from the Churches (Harvest Home and Sunday School exhibition, Princeton)
articles.author: J. P. C.
articles.summary: We had purposed in mind to furnish the readers of the Recorder with the first one of a series of articles on the Book Concern this week ... Last week, on Thursday, we attended a Harvest Home and Sunday School Exhibition at Princeton, on the Princeton circuit, under the charge of Rev. T. Gould. This proved to be another grand affair like the one the week previous at Trenton ... Addresses by Mr. Ven Horn, a young gentleman ... preparing for the work of the ministry, and by the writer, on the war and the coming end of slavery. Dated Trenton, August 21st [VERIFY], 1861.

articles.headline: The Harvest Home at Princeton
articles.author: T. Gould, for the Committee
articles.summary: Thanks to God, and kind friends, the Harvest Home came off at Princeton, on Thursday, the 15th inst., and proved to be a most pleasing affair. Kind Providence blessed us with a lovely day, and we had a large gathering, both of our citizens and the surrounding country for 20 miles in circumference ... we were addressed by Rev. J. P. Campbell, and Mr. M. Venhorn [VERIFY]. ... In the evening ... we had a Sabbath School exhibition in Mercer Hall ... We took in hand, on this occasion, about $110--we have cleared $75. Princeton, Aug. 20th, 1861.

articles.headline: News from the Churches (Cookstown, N.J. bush meeting)

Being previously solicited to attend a Bush Meeting in, or near said place, I accepted the entreaty. Leaving Philadelphia on Saturday afternoon, the 31st ult., in company with several friends, we arrived in Cookstown about 9 o'clock, P. M., and were conducted to a delightful grove, in which the meeting was being held. Our beloved brother, J. C. Cornish, of Bucks County Circuit, was dealing out the precious truths of the Gospel...
people: minister in charge, Bordentown and Allentown circuit (Cookstown society) (printed 'Wm. D. W. Schureman')

articles.headline: United Brothers and Sisters of Rev. Willis Nazrey Society (notice)
articles.author: Aaron Bell [VERIFY]
articles.summary: The United Brothers and Sisters of Rev. Willis Nazrey Society, are requested to attend their regular stated meeting, the 19th [VERIFY] of this month, at [hour illegible] o'clock, P. M., on the corner of Quince and Locust Streets. Punctual attendance is strictly requested, by order of the President.

articles.headline: A. M. E. Wesley Church Sabbath School (21st anniversary)
articles.summary: The twenty-first anniversary of the Sabbath School, connected with the A. M. E. Wesley church, Hurst street, Philadelphia, was held on Wednesday, the 4th inst., at Diamond Cottage, Camden, N. J. At 9 o'clock, A. M., the teachers of said school, and one hundred and twenty-five children, took their line of march from the church to the cottage...

articles.headline: Once More at Home
articles.author: E. Weaver
articles.summary: We would say to our numerous friends that we are once more, through the blessing of God, returned home and at our post. On our arrival we found, as usual, a large pile of letters, which we will give a careful perusal. We found Rev. A. L. Stanford and Mrs. Weaver to have been struggling for life to keep things as near right as possible until we returned...
people: kept the Book Concern going (wife of E. Weaver)

articles.headline: Religious Notices: Quarterly meetings on Salem Circuit; bush meeting at Dutchtown; quarterly meeting at New Brunswick
articles.author: T. W. Henry
articles.summary: Quarterly Meetings on Salem Circuit. On the 21st and 22d inst., at Dutchtown. On the 29th, at Salem. October 6th, at Frogtown. 13th, at Bucktown [VERIFY]. T. W. Henry, Minister. A Bush Meeting will be held at Dutchtown, commencing at 1 o'clock, P. M., on the 21st of September, and continue to the 23d. Quarterly Meeting will be held the 21st and 22d of this month, at New Brunswick, N. J. Peter Gardiner.
people: minister, New Brunswick N.J. (signer of quarterly-meeting notice)

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Nazrey
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor--Dear Sir:--I have just received a copy of the thirty-second number of your excellent paper, in which I see an article referring to myself in connexion with the B. M. E. Church in Canada. Sir, I shall not descend so low beneath the dignity of a Christian gentleman, as to enter into a newspaper war about church matters...
people: bishop; met Nazrey in Detroit (printed 'Bishop Quinn')

articles.headline: Death of Mr. Charles G. Parker (Banneker Institute resolutions)
articles.author: George T. Burrell
articles.summary: At a special meeting of the Banneker Institute, the death of Mr. Charles G. Parker having been announced, a committee of three, consisting of Messrs. K. Fauset [VERIFY], D. D. Turner and G. B. White [VERIFY], was appointed to draft resolutions of condolence with the family of the deceased...
people: deceased; member of the Banneker Institute
recording secretary, Banneker Institute (printed 'Jacob C. White, Jr., Rec. Sec.')

articles.headline: Appointments, Bethel Church (funeral sermon of Father Joshua Purnell)
articles.author: Joshua Woodlin
articles.summary: Sabbath morning at 10 o'clock. Afternoon at 3 o'clock, the funeral sermon of Father Joshua Purnell, by Elder Henry Davis, of Union Church. The relatives, members of the church, the class of which he was a member, the bands of which he was Father, and the friends generally, are respectfully invited to attend on the occasion. In the evening at 7 1/2 o'clock, Elder A. L. Stanford, of Little Wesley Church. Joshua Woodlin, Minister in Charge.
people: deceased; Bethel member, 'Father' of the bands (printed 'Father Joshua Purnell')
preacher of funeral sermon, Elder, of Union Church
evening preacher, Elder, of Little Wesley Church

articles.headline: A Call
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: Dear Bro. Stanford:--As a minister of the A. M. E. Church, I rejoice to see the intellectual advancement and the literary progress of our Church. In the language of Isaiah, 'A little one shall become a thousand...' Sir, I view the Christian Recorder as the voice of our people--as the representative of the Church...

articles.headline: The Ministry We Want
articles.author: J. P. C.
articles.summary: We have recently had reason to hope, that amid the general corruption of these corrupting times, there are still to be found in the church, men who are willing to forsake all, and labor for good and godliness sake... Such are the men we want, and such are the men we must have to fill the pulpit of the A. M. E. Church in America. (Trenton, September 9th [VERIFY], 1861.)

articles.headline: Henry Floyd, Grocer (Fine Groceries for Family Use)
articles.summary: Fine Groceries for Family Use. Henry Floyd, Grocer and Dealer in Choice Teas, Coffees, Spices, &c., No. 407 South Twelfth Street, below Pine, Philadelphia.
people: grocer, No. 407 South Twelfth Street below Pine

articles.headline: Religious Notices: Wesley Church and Bethel Church appointments; National Fast Day services
articles.author: Joshua Woodlin
articles.summary: Appointments in the A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst St., Philadelphia, viz: Sunday morning, 10 1/2 o'clock; afternoon at 3 [VERIFY] o'clock--subject, 'The Sea of Glass;' evening, 7 1/2 o'clock--sermon by Rev. E. Weaver. 'The President of the United States has appointed the last Thursday of September to be observed as a day of humiliation, prayer, and fasting;' in accordance with the same, Divine services will be held, viz: on Thursday, the 26th, at 10 o'clock, A. M., in Bethel Church--sermon by Rev. E. Weaver, General Book Steward. Rev. J. Woodlin, Pastor...
people: pastor, A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst St.; fast-day preacher
preacher, Bethel, Sabbath evening 22 Sept (Rev.), of the New York Conference

articles.headline: An Obituary of the Life and Happy Death of Mr. Joshua Pernal
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: He was born a slave on the eastern shore of Maryland, in the year of our Lord, 1769, and lived there until the year of our Lord, 1810, during which time he married a wife--she being also a slave. They had several children, and he, through industry, having purchased the freedom of his wife and children, brought them to Philadelphia. He being set free, then went back to Maryland, stayed seven years, then came back to Philadelphia in the year 1817, and joined the A. M. E. Bethel Church...
people: deceased 15 July 1861, aged 92 years lacking one month; Bethel member from 1817; second father of the bands of Bethel Church

articles.headline: News from the Churches: A Member of the Church at Trenton Burned to Death
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Sister Caroline Taylor, a member of the A. M. E. Mount Zion Church, of our charge, in the city of Trenton, has been burned to death. This dreadful calamity occurred in the following manner: On Monday morning last, a week ago to-day, being September 9th, 1861, Sister Taylor arose at 4 o'clock in the morning to commence her daily labor at the place where she was living at service...
people: deceased; member of A.M.E. Mount Zion Church, Trenton; burned to death while in service, died in her 22d year
preacher of the sermon she heard the evening before (printed 'Brother Joseph Long')

articles.headline: Religious Notices: A. M. E. Wesley Church (funeral sermon of Sister Eliza Sipple)
articles.summary: A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst St., Sunday morning, 10 1/2 o'clock; afternoon, 3 o'clock, the funeral sermon of Sister Eliza Sipple will be delivered; evening, 7 1/2 o'clock, the Rev. J. R. V. Morgan is expected to preach.
people: deceased; funeral sermon at A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst St. (printed 'Sister Eliza Sipple')

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Conference and Quarterly Meetings, Bordentown and Freehold Circuits
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: Quarterly Conference of the Bordentown Circuit, to be held at Allentown, October 19th, [hour] o'clock, P. M. Quarterly Meetings:--Allentown, Oct. 20th; Bordentown, Oct. 27th; Cookstown, Nov. 3d; Cranberry, Nov. 10th. The Quarterly Conference of the Freehold Circuit to be held at Riceville [VERIFY], November 16th, 3 o'clock, P. M. W. D. W. Schureman, Minister.

articles.headline: Notice: Quarterly Meetings, Burlington circuit
articles.author: J. H. Smith
articles.summary: Quarterly Meeting at Burlington on the first Sabbath of October. At Mount Holly on the second Sabbath of October. At Evesham on the third Sabbath of October. At Milford on the fourth Sabbath of October. At Snow Hill, first Sabbath of November. At Jordantown, second Sabbath of November. J. H. Smith, Elder in Charge.

articles.headline: Notice: Association of Alumni of the Institute for Colored Youth formed
articles.summary: At a meeting of the graduates of the Institute for Colored Youth, held at the Institute Building, September 19th, 1861, an Association of Alumni was formed, and the following named elected permanent officers: President--Octavius V. Catto. Vice President--Estellena [VERIFY] Johnson. Rec. Sec.--Wm. T. Jones. Cor. Sec.--Henry Boyer [VERIFY], Jr. Treas.--Joseph B. [VERIFY] White. Executive Council...

articles.headline: Sabbath School Anniversary (A. M. E. Mission Church, Philadelphia)
articles.summary: On Thursday, the 5th inst., the Sabbath-School of the A. M. E. Mission Church, Philadelphia, celebrated their annual festival at Diamond Cottage, Camden, N. J. An address was ably delivered to an immense audience, by the Rev. Stephen Smith, after which the choir and pupils seemed to charm the listeners with their sweet chants of sacred music, which cannot be easily surpassed. N. B.--The printing of the above has been delayed by unavoidable circumstances.--Ed.

events.name: Quarterly meeting, A. M. E. Union Church, Coates Street
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meeting announced for July 20th and 21st, 1861, by Henry Davis, Minister. A separate notice in the same column gives the minister's residence as No. 114 Eutaw street, between Race and Cherry streets, and between 7th and 8th, Philadelphia.
attendees: minister, A. M. E. Union Church; residence No. 114 Eutaw street

events.name: First quarterly meeting, Zion Mission, Philadelphia
events.location: Zion Mission, Philadelphia
events.description: The First Quarterly meeting for Zion Mission, Philadelphia, to be held the 20th of July, 1861. Signed Stephen Smith, Pastor.

events.name: Allentown Circuit (N.J.) quarterly conference and quarterly meetings
events.location: Bordentown, Cookstown, Allentown and Cramberry, N.J.
events.description: Quarterly Conference at Bordentown, 3 o'clock P. M., July 13th, 1861; quarterly meetings at Bordentown July 14, Cookstown July 21, Allentown July 28, Cramberry August 4. Signed W. D. W. Scheroman [VERIFY: surname imperfectly printed], Minister.
attendees: minister, Allentown Circuit (printed 'Wm. D. W. Schureman')

events.name: Quarterly meeting and love-feast, Little Wesley Church
events.location: Little Wesley Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Little Wesley Church on Sunday the 14th inst.; love-feast Monday night the 15th, doors open at 8 o'clock and close at 9. Signed A. L. Stanford, Minister. The same column gives Stanford's office hours at Little Wesley Church, Hurst Street: Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, 9 to 11 A. M.

events.name: United Brothers and Sisters of Rev. Willis Nazrey Society -- stated meeting
events.location: corner of Quince and Locust Streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Regular stated meeting called for the 15th of July at 8 o'clock P. M., corner of Quince and Locust Streets; punctual attendance requested by order of the President. Aaron Hall, President; E. Maloney [VERIFY], Secretary.

events.name: First quarterly meeting of the conference year, Trenton Circuit
events.location: Trenton, N.J.
events.description: Reported by J. P. Campbell (Trenton, July 8th, 1861): First Quarterly Meeting at Trenton on Friday, Saturday and Sabbath, July 5th, 6th and 7th. Friday evening general class meeting; Saturday the Quarterly Conference (all members present save three) and preaching by brother Long, a local preacher of the circuit; Sabbath 9 o'clock love-feast, 11 o'clock sacramental discourse by the pastor, 3 o'clock service; at night 'that venerable old servant of God, Mr. George McMullin [VERIFY]' preached. Campbell also reports on the Philadelphia Conference session that met May 18th.

events.name: Bush meeting at South Camden for the A. M. E. Mission at Kaighnsville
events.location: South Camden, N.J. (near Kaighn's Point); evening services at Macedonia Church
events.description: Bush meeting on Sabbath July 21st, 1861, from 10 o'clock; preaching at 10, 2 and 4 o'clock by Revs. Thomas Cooper, James Fuller [VERIFY], Joshua Woodlin and Elisha Weaver; collection for the A. M. E. Mission at Kaighnsville; services continuing in the evening at the Macedonia Church. Philadelphians directed to the ferry boats from the upper side of South Street to Kaighn's Point, every fifteen minutes. Notice signed T. Cooper.

events.name: Princeton Circuit first quarterly meeting
events.location: Princeton, N.J.
events.description: Reported by J. P. Campbell (Trenton, July 16th [VERIFY], 1861). Quarterly Conference Saturday afternoon July 13 with Rev. T. Gould, preacher in charge, and all members present; Saturday evening discourse by brother Andrew Hattle [VERIFY]; Sunday love-feast (people present from all appointments on the circuit and from the Trenton and New Brunswick circuits), 11 o'clock discourse on Isaiah liii. 7 and the Lord's Supper, 3 o'clock sermon by Rev. T. Gould on justification by faith (Romans v. 1), evening discourse to young men; twelve came forward for prayers.

events.name: Love-feast at Little Wesley Church
events.location: Little Wesley Church, Hurst street, Philadelphia
events.description: Weaver reports that on Monday night (July 15) Rev. A. L. Stanford held his love-feast at Little Wesley Church in Hurst street; Stanford read the fourth chapter of the first epistle of John and called on Weaver to pray; bread and water passed around. Same report: Weaver's visit to Burlington quarterly meeting (Sabbath July 7, Rev. Joseph Smith, elder in charge); Stanford introduced at the printing office to Mr. Young, Mr. Blakely and others; Bordentown quarterly meeting July 13-14 with 'our Rev. Brother Schureman' (church with a basement story; all papers and many hymn books sold; Mr. and Mrs. Collins met, Mrs. Collins teacher of the public school).

events.name: Quarterly meeting, Bethel A. M. E. Church
events.location: A. M. E. Bethel Church, Sixth street, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meeting on Sabbath July 28, 1861: general class Friday night; preaching Saturday night at 8; band love-feast Sunday 5 A. M.; preaching at 10 by Rev. S. Holcomb [VERIFY], at 3 by Rev. T. H. Cooper [VERIFY initials], minister in charge of Camden Station, and at a quarter to 8 by A. L. Stanford, elder in charge of Little Wesley; love-feast Monday night (doors 7 to 9). Notice signed J. Woodlin, Elder in charge (of Bethel).
attendees: preacher (Rev.); minister in charge of Camden Station
preacher; elder in charge of Little Wesley

events.name: Burlington A. M. E. Sabbath School annual picnic
events.location: "Fountain Woods" [VERIFY], near Burlington, N.J.
events.description: Annual picnic of the Sabbath School of the Burlington A. M. E. Church, Thursday August 1, 1861 (West India Emancipation day), on the grounds known as 'Fountain Woods' [VERIFY] near Burlington. Signed Jos. S. Smith [VERIFY], in charge (the Book Steward's report of 07-20 calls the Burlington elder 'Rev. Joseph Smith').

events.name: Pennington (N.J.) quarterly meeting
events.location: Pennington, N.J.
events.description: Reported by J. P. Campbell. Quarterly meeting Saturday and Sunday July 20-21, 1861, with general class Friday evening; Saturday sermon by brother J. Long on Spiritual Sight; Sunday love-feast; 11 o'clock sermon by Rev. J. G. Bulaugh [VERIFY], an aged worn-out itinerant who spent a week on the charge (Gen. xxii. 9, 'Isaac a type of Christ'); 3 o'clock sermon by Rev. T. Gould; 8 o'clock evening discourse by the writer to the young men of the place.

events.name: Sermon course on affliction, Little Wesley Chapel
events.location: Little Wesley Chapel, Philadelphia
events.description: First sermon of a course on affliction delivered at Little Wesley Chapel, Sabbath July 28, 1861, 10 A.M. ('the 28th inst.' as printed; the 28th of July). Preacher not named. The next sermon of the course was announced for the next Sabbath afternoon (Aug. 4) at 3 o'clock, subject 'The Stones of the Heavenly Temple prepared on Earth.'

events.name: Quarterly meeting, Rocky Hill, Princeton Circuit (N.J.)
events.location: Rocky Hill, Princeton Circuit, New Jersey
events.description: Quarterly meeting July 27-28, 1861 attended and reported by J. P. Campbell (letter dated Trenton, July 30). Saturday evening Campbell preached (Acts xxiv. 16); Sabbath 9 a.m. love feast; 11 a.m. sermon and holy communion; 3 P.M. Rev. T. Gould, pastor of the circuit, preached on Joshua i. 11. Conference affiliation of the Princeton Circuit not stated in the item.

events.name: Grand Tabernacle of Pennsylvania, Grand United Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity -- annual commencement and installation
events.location: the Tabernacle, Lombard Street, west of Seventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Annual Commencement (Friday, date not stated) of the Grand Tabernacle of the State of Pennsylvania. Officers installed by Brother John H. Hughes, G. G. D. M.: G. W. G. S., Bro. Benjamin Nixon; G. W. I. G.(?), Bro. Henry H. Draper; G. W. Con., Bro. Josiah Cornelius; G. W. Chaplain, Bro. Elisha [surname illegible, looks like 'Wonham']; G. W. Treas., Bro. Geo. W. Hollingsworth [VERIFY]; G. W. A. S., Sister Anna E. Biddle [VERIFY]; G. W. Scribe, Bro. Wm. D. Cooper; G. D. W. S. (or O. G. W. S.), Bro. Geo. W. [surname illegible: 'Dernias' on 08-03, 'Hausee' on 08-10]; G. W. V. S., Sister Emma W. Hemmenway [VERIFY]; G. W. S., Rev. Bro. Wm. D. W. Schureman. Grand Executive Committee: Sisters Susan Steele [VERIFY], Mary Jackson, Anna B. Lancaster [VERIFY]; Bros. Wm. H. Draper and Solomon F. Mitchell. Grand Worthy Superior Rev. William D. W. Schureman appointed district aids: Southern District, Wm. H. Thomas, Washington, D.C.; Western District, Rt. Rev. Brother J. J. Clinton; New England District, Rev. Brother William Jackson; Eastern District, Rev. Brother Jacob R. (or H.) Trusty; California, Rev. Brother Chas. J. Carter [VERIFY]. General Degree Department: Grand General Degree Master John H. Hughes appointed Brother William D. Cooper, Assistant Degree Master, and Sisters Sarah Ann Johnson and Emma L. Jackson, Assistant General Degree Mistresses. Published by order of the G. Tabernacle: John H. Hughes, [given name illegible] Johnson, Wm. D. Cooper, Committee. (District aids outside Philadelphia are not linked.)
attendees: Grand General Degree Master; installing officer
G. W. Scribe; Assistant Degree Master
Grand Worthy Superior (Rev.) (printed 'Wm. D. W. Schureman')

events.location: corner of Quince and Locust Streets, Philadelphia
events.description: The United Brothers and Sisters of Rev. Willis Nazrey Society are requested to attend their regular stated meeting, the 19th of this month (August 19, 1861), at 8 o'clock P.M., at the corner of Quince and Locust Streets. Punctual attendance strictly requested by order of the President. Signed Aaron Bell [VERIFY], President; E. Maloney [VERIFY], Secretary.

events.name: Parker T. Smith leaves Philadelphia for Canada West
events.location: Philadelphia to Chatham and Dresden, Canada West
events.description: Parker T. Smith, formerly of Philadelphia and author of a series of ethnological articles in the Christian Recorder, left Philadelphia Friday afternoon, July 5, 1861 ('5th ult.'), at a quarter past 3, arriving at Chatham, C.W., on Sunday morning; writes from Dresden, C.W., Aug. 2, 1861, his chosen new home. Reports a flourishing colored Odd Fellows lodge (Prince Albert Lodge) at Dresden, news intended for 'members of the Order in Philadelphia'.
attendees: emigrant from Philadelphia to Dresden, C.W.; letter writer

events.name: Harvest Home, Trenton (announced)
events.location: Trenton, N.J.
events.description: A grand Harvest Home to be held in Trenton under the pastoral charge of Rev. J. P. Campbell, on Thursday the 8th (printed '8th ult.', but Thursday the 8th is August 8, 1861); the notice arrived too late for publication.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at 'Louisville' [VERIFY], Philadelphia District
events.location: Louisville [VERIFY] (place in J. P. Campbell's district; state not given)
events.description: Quarterly meeting held 'Sunday last' (probably Aug. 4, 1861), reported by J. P. C., corresponding editor of the Philadelphia District. Crowd too large for the building; services held outdoors. Morning sermon by the aged local preacher Rev. George M'Mollin [VERIFY] on 'See that ye fall not out by the way'; in the afternoon Campbell preached on the chief priests' counsel against Jesus.

events.name: Fourth sermon of the course on affliction, Wesley Church, Hurst Street
events.location: Wesley church, Hurst street, Philadelphia
events.description: Sabbath evening, August 18, 1861 ('the 18th inst.'): fourth sermon of the course (on Christ holding the keys of death and hell) delivered at Wesley Church, Hurst Street, to the largest congregation of the series. Followed by an exhortation by Rev. J. R. V. Morgan and prayer by Rev. H. Davis; about three persons professed conviction. The preacher of the course is not named. Next sermon announced for the next Sabbath evening (Aug. 25) at 8 o'clock: 'The Weaned Child.'

events.name: Harvest Home and Sabbath School exhibition, Princeton (N.J.)
events.location: woods near Princeton; evening exhibition in Mercer Hall, Princeton, N.J.
events.description: Harvest Home of the Princeton circuit (pastor Rev. T. Gould), Thursday, August 15, 1861: large gathering from 20 miles around, dinner in the woods, addresses by Rev. J. P. Campbell (on the war and the end of slavery) and Mr. M. Venhorn [VERIFY] (a young man preparing for the ministry), and an evening Sabbath School exhibition in Mercer Hall. Receipts about $110, cleared $75, toward completing a new church edifice; reported by T. Gould for the Committee (Princeton, Aug. 20) and by J. P. C. (Trenton). Campbell refers to a similar Harvest Home at Trenton the week before.

events.name: Fifth and last sermon of the affliction course, A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street
events.location: A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst street, Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday evening, August 25, 1861: fifth and last sermon of the course on affliction ('The Weaned Child', Ps. cxxxi. 2), to a large, quiet and attentive audience. Series ran Sabbaths July 28 (Little Wesley Chapel), Aug. 4 and Aug. 11 (announced), Aug. 18 and Aug. 25 (Wesley Church, Hurst St.). Preacher never named in the synopses.

events.name: A. M. E. Sabbath School celebration excursion to Spring Mill
events.location: Spring Mill station (cars from Eighteenth and Market streets, Philadelphia)
events.description: Celebration of the [Horn?]town [VERIFY] Sabbath School of the A. M. E. Church, first Thursday in September 1861 (September 5). Addresses by Rev. J. H. Smith and others. Cars leaving Eighteenth and Market streets at 7 A.M. for Spring Mill station. Notice signed J. W. Johnson [VERIFY], Minister in Charge.

events.name: Funeral of Mary Ann Parker
events.location: not stated
events.description: Mary Ann, daughter of Nathaniel and Mary Parker [VERIFY], died August 17, 1861, aged eleven years three months, after visits from 'our old experienced mothers in Israel'. The Sabbath School under the charge of Rev. Richard Robinson [VERIFY] attended the funeral; a discourse was delivered and the school sang a hymn at the grave. Place of residence/church not stated.
attendees: minister in charge of the Sabbath School (Rev.)

events.name: Bush meeting at Cookstown, N.J. (A.M.E.)
events.location: grove at or near Cookstown, N.J.
events.description: Bush meeting Saturday 31 Aug - Monday 2 Sept 1861 to raise repairs money for the A.M.E. church at Cookstown, N.J. Writer (unsigned; probably acting editor A. L. Stanford, to whom a quoted letter is addressed) left Philadelphia Sat. 31 Aug with several friends. Saturday night: J. C. Cornish of Bucks County Circuit preaching to 300-400. Sabbath 10:30 a.m.: Rev. Jabez P. Campbell (Luke 14:17); 3 p.m.: the writer (Luke 8:5); 8 p.m.: Rev. J. R. V. Morgan, 'The World's Harvest' (Rev. 14:14-15). Two to three thousand present at each Sabbath meeting. Monday 9 a.m. service; concluded 10:30 a.m. The Cookstown society has thirteen members yet raised '$60, and over'; it is in connexion with Bordentown and Allentown and served by Wm. D. W. Schureman. Writer sold 50 copies of the Christian Recorder there; returned to Philadelphia Monday 11 a.m.
attendees: minister of the circuit (printed 'Wm. D. W. Schureman')

events.name: United Brothers and Sisters of Rev. Willis Nazrey Society -- stated meeting
events.location: corner of Quince and Locust Streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Regular stated meeting of the United Brothers and Sisters of Rev. Willis Nazrey Society, 'the 19th [VERIFY] of this month' (September 1861), P.M., at the corner of Quince and Locust Streets. Signed Aaron Bell [VERIFY], President; secretary's name illegible (E. or R. M--oney/Maloney?). Repeated 09-14.

events.name: Wesley A.M.E. Church (Hurst St.) Sabbath School -- 21st anniversary excursion
events.location: Diamond Cottage, Camden, N.J.
events.description: Twenty-first anniversary of the Sabbath School of the A.M.E. Wesley church, Hurst street, Philadelphia. 9 a.m.: teachers and 125 children marched from the church to Diamond Cottage, Camden, accompanied by many adults. 2 p.m. [hour reading uncertain]: managers and teachers spread a table in the grove; more than 200 children and 100 adults fed. 3 p.m.: more than 1,500 persons heard addresses by Revs. Joshua Woodlyn, J. R. V. Morgan and T. H. Cooper. Praise given to the superintendent, Mr. John H. Hughes, and his assistants.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's preaching appointments, north-western Philadelphia District
events.location: Montrose and Abington Centre (Pa.), then Reading
events.description: In his letter dated Chatham, C.W., Sept. 3, 1861, Bishop W. Nazrey says he had intended to begin work in the north-western portion of the Philadelphia District about the first of the month but is detained by legal matters. Appointments: preach at Montrose the evening of 23 Oct; Abington Centre the 24th; the Elder to arrange the rest of the circuit until the 31st, when he leaves for Reading; 'Brother Logan' to make the appointments for his circuit until 7 Nov and meet him at Reading. If he misses the cars he will preach at Abington the 24th and 25th. The letter rebuts a critic in the B.M.E. Church (Canada) controversy, naming A. R. Green, C. H. Pearce and G. W. Brodie [Canadian, not linked], and notes he left Boston in July for the Indiana Conference but abandoned the trip after meeting Bishop Quinn in Detroit.

events.name: Banneker Institute -- special meeting on the death of Charles G. Parker
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Special meeting of the Banneker Institute on the announced death of fellow member Mr. Charles G. Parker. Committee of three (Messrs. K. Fauset [VERIFY], D. D. Turner, G. B. White [VERIFY]) drafted a preamble and resolutions of condolence to his widow and fatherless children; resolved a copy be sent to the family and published in the Christian Recorder. Signed George T. Burrell, President; attest, Jacob C. White, Jr., Rec. Sec. Date of meeting not printed.

events.name: Bethel Church -- funeral sermon of Father Joshua Purnell
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Sabbath appointments at Bethel (the Sabbath following the 14 Sept. issue): 10 a.m. service; 3 p.m. funeral sermon of Father Joshua Purnell by Elder Henry Davis of Union Church, relatives, church members, his class and the bands (of which he was Father) invited; 7:30 p.m. Elder A. L. Stanford of Little Wesley Church. Joshua Woodlin, Minister in Charge.

events.name: National Fast Day services at Bethel and Wesley (A.M.E.) churches, with collection for the Book Concern
events.location: Bethel Church and A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst St., Philadelphia
events.description: For the national day of humiliation, prayer and fasting appointed by President Lincoln (last Thursday of September, the 26th): 10 a.m. at Bethel Church, sermon by Rev. E. Weaver, General Book Steward (notice signed Rev. J. Woodlin, Pastor); 3 p.m. [hour partly legible] at the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst St., sermon on the position the colored people of the United States should occupy in the present crisis, by the pastor, A. L. Stanford. A collection to be taken that day in each of the above churches as a free-will offering to the A.M.E. Book Concern, to be continued in the evening at Bethel Church. Weaver's 'Read This Everybody' (same page) asks all preachers to make the fast day a free-will offering for the Book Concern.

events.name: Sabbath appointments, Bethel and Wesley churches

events.name: Death of Joshua Pernal (Purnell), Bethel Church
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: Obituary by Henry Davis, Elder of the A.M.E. Union Church, Phila. Joshua Pernal was born a slave on the Eastern Shore of Maryland in 1769 and lived there until 1810; married a wife, also a slave; they had several children. Through industry he purchased the freedom of his wife and children and brought them to Philadelphia; being himself set free, he went back to Maryland for seven years, returned to Philadelphia in 1817 and joined Bethel Church, remaining a member while he lived. Member of the spiritual bands of his church from their origin; appointed and elected second father of the bands of Bethel Church in 1858 [VERIFY year] and continued while he lived. Enjoyed religion sixty years or more. Died 15 July 1861, aged 92 years lacking one month. The same man as 'Father Joshua Purnell' whose funeral sermon Elder Henry Davis preached at Bethel (CR 1861-09-14 p2).
attendees: author, Elder of the A.M.E. Union Church, Phila.

events.name: Death of Caroline Taylor, Mount Zion A.M.E. Church, Trenton
events.location: Trenton, N.J.
events.description: Report 'from our Corresponding Editor of the Philadelphia District', signed J. P. Campbell, Trenton, Sep. 17th, 1861. Sister Caroline Taylor, member of the A.M.E. Mount Zion Church, Trenton (Campbell's charge), living at service, rose at 4 a.m. on Monday 9 Sept. 1861 and poured burning fluid on a slow kitchen-stove fire; the can exploded and her clothes caught fire. The master of the house shut the bed-chamber door on her; she rolled in the yard; he then threw water on her and wrapped her in a blanket. She was taken to the house of her brother-in-law, Brother Lewis Green, and after twenty-eight hours died at 9 o'clock Tuesday morning (printed 'September 11th'), in her twenty-second year. Leaves an aged mother, two or three sisters and other relatives. The evening before, she had heard a sermon on the day of judgment by Brother Joseph Long, with an exhortation by Father McMullen [VERIFY], and resolved to return to her class. Campbell attended her death-bed.
attendees: pastor, Mount Zion A.M.E. Church, Trenton; attended her
